ratings.comment: Nobody can understand her class
Susan Nachwati has enlightened me throughout fall semester. She helped me succeed in every possible ways. without her i would be failing

Ignore the bad rating; she's kind & nice. Shes not disorganized, yet she teaches a lot of classes & she gives plenty of work for you to understand the material. Yet her office hours are always open to students & she will go beyond her limits to teach you the material. ASK questions and go to classes to learn; otherwise, it will be a bit hard.

Don't take this class if you're new to python. You will be confused. Only reason I passed was because I had prior experience with coding/python. She doesn't respond to emails and grading takes forever. I gave up paying attention in class by the 2nd week and just did homework. Pros is she's a light grader and doesn't care if you submit work late.
Susan ain't that bad. I lowkenuinely thought I was gonna end up with a B but she ended up giving 200% on my Lab and ended up with an A on her class. She's so misunderstood

It's an easy class with a nice prof and pretty lenient grading... but my god it is disorganized.

She admitted at one point she doesn't plan out lectures, but plans the topics and codes as she talks. Grading is unclear and takes forever, lab and lecture are very disconnected/no communication, and I've never seen a teacher with more tech issues.

It was an easy class and I still have no clue what is it actually about. The midterm and final were fairly easy. At the end, she gave a ton of extra credits. Also she doesn't really mind late submission.

She's a nice person but so-so as a professor. It was my first time learning Python and it was way better than I expected. However, her lecture and lab activity can be a bit messy. She will probably let you out late every single class meeting. Also a lot of homework but she will extend the deadline if you ask but you have to constantly remind her.
Susan cares about your success and I feel that a caring professor is something rare nowadays. Just go to her office hours if youre struggling

ngl, this class was hard at first, but once you enter into a state flow you will understand the materials of the class. Most people cheated on the exams so I supposed exams are easy to do. Just dont forget to do her quizzes

If you have no experience in python, then DO NOT take her class whatsoever. Even though she's a great professor, her lectures are messy and sometimes she won't respond to your email. Zybooks is your best friend, but the projects are very tough. There are only 2 exams and a final so make sure you study hard and don't procrastinate.

If you don't know programming, DON'T take this class. Susan is so disorganized; lectures jump around and include tangents on languages we don't use. Don't expect to learn. She takes attendance sporadically to ensure attendance, but it's partially because she always just forgets. The projects are time consuming and the instructions are unclear.

If you have no experience of python, you are so cooked. I fought for my life in this class and didn't learn anything unfortunately, only learned a little bit through zybooks. The professor doesn't really know how to teach. She's pretty nice, but that's it. TA didn't really help either, but she tried. We had abt 5 projects with a partner in our lab.

Very sweet professor however her lectures can be a bit messy and unorganized. Zybook will be your friend when it comes to learning the material. Communication with her is difficult, I once emailed her about my absence and I never got a response. Not that bad of a class to take you just really need to put in the work and attend office hours.

She is a really nice prof but her lectures are unorganized for an introduction class. Most of the people who are giving her 5 stars most likely have had experience in coding. You will end up finding yourself self-teaching most of the material. Her grading system is also a little silly. Don't take her if you have no experience in python!!!

Dr. Nachawati shines above all my other professors. She is so approachable and kind. Definitely go to office hours because they are super important for understanding hard topics and getting a good grade. She is extremely helpful one-on-one and truly cares about your success. She is just wonderful.

Dr. Nachawati is honestly the sweetest professor ever. She is so thoughtful and incredibly patient with everyone. You should definitely go to her office hours because they are super important and she is extremely helpful one-on-one. She genuinely cares about her students and really wants to see every person succeed

Dr. Nachawati lwky underrated but be ready to grind. She teaches super well, but assigns tons of HW and quizzes. You HAVE to participate in class too. Not an easy A, but you'll actually learn. Highly recommend if you're willing to put in the work

Dr. Susan Nachawati is hands down one of the best professors I have encountered. If you actually want to learn the material and leave the course with a solid understanding of the subject, take her class. She is engaging, incredibly knowledgeable, and explains complex concepts with somewhat of a clarity
she's tough at grading but her class is easy ash. Idk why people are hating on her, she's underrated.

she's slow at grading but she's an okay professor. I wouldn't take this class if you don't have prior knowledge in CS, but if you do you should take her. Her lab is easy to understand but her lecture, not so much. Go to her office hours if youre struggling

Susan Nachawati is a misunderstood professor. Once you get along with her, you will begin to thrive in her class. Most people are just hating just because they don't understand her. In my humble opinion, Susan Nachawati is someone that I would be delighted to have. She also offers me redemption and extra credit whenever I go to her office hours.

She is sososo sweet and kind and cares about her students. but... honestly her teaching style/lectures arent good ESPECIALLY if you havent coded before taking this class like me. Her labs are way ahead her homework on zybook which is what actually teaches you the material well. Labs arent too bad but can be hard if you fall behind.

I marked hilarious because her ability to communicate with students is geneuinely so awful to the point where you can't not laugh at this class. She doesn't provide any midterm dates until a week before the exam. You technically don't even need to attend her lectures because everyone seems to be learning from the onlline textbook assignments.

Susan is not even that bad. Go to her office hour because she will help you the most there. People here are just clueless of what they're doing hence why they're struggling. Overall, take her if you're a CS major and you're good at coding

Every morning before this class, I would fantasize crashing my car on the 405. She never grades anything so we don't know our actual grade in the class. Her lectures are way too messy. She shows up late to her own lectures yet expects you to be here on time. This class suck bootyhole.

Avoid her if you're new to programming. Her lectures are messy and confusing, straying off topic to mention her son and his work. For a professor in a tech field, she often had trouble navigating lecture with her iPad. Be ready to teach yourself with ZyBook but if you know python well you'll be fine. She's the reason why I changed my major.

Genuinely made me want to switch majors. she got switched into my chosen class TWICE. 45 mins for the midterm, and she gets mad if you ask her questions. I learned because of my lab TA and zybooks. She will never answer your emails, and she should not be an advisor.

Terrible. Didn't show our grades for the final. Went from a 89% to a C in my transcript. She removed our access to the class before the final day as well. I emailed her and got a response once the semester ended and she said nothing can be done. Grading criteria will throw you off because syllabus will say one thing and your grade will another

Definitely would take Susan again. She made 225 super easy. I will say the only thing is attendance is mandatory but for this type of class, I see why. Her exams are super easy but even if you fail them, their really not heavy in canvas so you will be fine. Take her! She'll adore and want the best for you!

She was a decent prof, but was completely unorganized, gets off topic during lectures, and kind of boring. Attendance is 100% mandatory. She doesn't read her emails well, like there's no point emailing her at all. If you don't care and want an easy A in this class, take her. Midterm was open note/internet. Final was to write a 1000 word essay.

It's funny to me how convoluted and all over the place she is... with a 1 unit class. In the midterm she showed up 10 minutes late and took another 10 minutes to assign it online because ironically, cannot navigate Canvas

Announcements about class are posted 10 minutes before class starts and very misleading and uninformed. Will waste your time 99% of mandatory class days. May seem nice but does not care about students at all and useless teacher that has no idea what shes talking about.

I thought the one-stars were exaggerating, but she is extremely disorganized, changes due dates without telling us, and refuses to answer emails. On top of that, attendance is mandatory and for nothing really.

Susan Nachawati is all over the place, never gives clear instructions, goes over class time, and is not very good at responding to emails. Attendance will make or break your grade and the lectures are pretty boring. She seems nice and funny at first but often goes off topic, talking about anything but the lecture.

It's unfortunate that she's the only professor that teaches assembly at the college that I go to. Nobody has any clue on to what their grade is as she has assignments and tests ungraded since october. Lectures are very loosely connected to what is on the exams inaccessible out of class, doesn't follow through with what she says, answer keys wrong

Professor Susan is one of those professor that tries her best to teach a comp sci class. It is very difficult teaching a comp sci class so I understand why she has 1 star ratings. It is up to you as an individual to put in the work outside of class and study Zybook hard to pass this class. I highly recommend making friends in this class for help.

She's nice, but if you don't put in the effort you will struggle and are better off not taking her. Go to office hours. Ask questions in class. Talk to her for clarification after lectures. Show that you do want to pass, and you will. She rounded my grade (which honestly shouldn't have been) to a next-letter grade because I did all of the above.

Grading is ridiculous. Changed grading system at end of semester which was supposed to "help" students' grades and instead dropped everyone grade ~4-8%. Would have had an A had previous system remained. Doen't reopen work for anyone, typically fair however I was ill and provided doctor's/hospital signatures and still refusing all semester. Awful

Messy, unorganized, hw-excessive course. Excessive project reports. (One was assigned over break). Good thing is that exams + quizzes are a small % of ur grade and they aren't too difficult. She also curves hw; do the work and you'll be fine. Overall, she's caring but lectures are boring, there's too much work and canvas is a pain to deal with.
Tuff teacher

She is honestly a great person and still held lecture even though she was going through a lot at home as she shared. She is just not a good teacher. Her lectures were disorganized and we did not learn as much as we should have. This wouldn't be a problem if attendance wasn't a part of the grade, but it is. Most of the learning will be on ZyBooks.

During the semester, Professor Nachawati's lectures and the lab activities afterward never seemed to line up in content. Students were better off learning from the ZyLabs and YouTube videos rather than her lectures. She seems to ramble a lot or make mistakes in her code where students were the ones having to correct her.

The professor tries hard, but the class can be disorganized. Attendance is mandatory, and you'll need to put in extra effort, like using tools like unstuck ai, to stay on top of things. Overall, a challenging but manageable course.

Prof. Nachawati is nice however she is very unprofessional and makes the lectures drag. She often talks about one singular subject while overcomplicating it and also giving no notice on any assignments. If you have her expect to do the entirety of your learning online and pay attention to assignments on canvas as she locks them if they're past due.

She's teaching multiple classes at multiple colleges. I took her elsewhere, & while she is kind, she struggled to respond to emails timely & grade assignments. Attendance is mandatory, but I only attended for exams & was not dropped. I self taught the material. Easy if you have prior knowledge of binary/hex/discrete structures. Good luck otherwise.

She is a nice teacher, but she gets lost in her lectures, and you are better off reading ZyBooks. Students made a lot of corrections during the lecture. Being at 8 am, this class made it so unmotivating to show up, but attendance was mandatory.
Susan is a nice, knowledgeable professor but is unorganized and unable to translate the material taught in the lectures into something learnable. You're better off learning from the Zybooks.

Only reason she's not a 1 is because she allowed cheat sheets for the midterm and final. Very disorganized and often incoherent. You realistically only learn from the ZyBook, which is very annoying and tedious. The wording on her tests is really confusing. Also, the extra credit she gives brings your grade down :). Avoid this professor if you can.
Take this class if you want inconsistent grading and a headache.

She's a really nice person. However she is so unorganized, would bounce around topics and always go on tangents. Communication was almost non existent, wouldn't reply to emails, wouldn't give due dates, would cancel class and not let you know until 20 min before. Attendance is mandatory but she'd be late almost every class. Horrible.

She is very non organized and just jumps between subjects out of nowhere. She is not clear with assignments and doesn't accept late work. She is most of the time late to class and she left the states for a week when there is two weeks left of the semester. Her tests were basic but sometimes the coding questions would break and had to restart it.

She is VERY smart but unorganized, there were no clear due dates for many of the assignments but no late work was accepted. She was often late to classes, and lectures/assignments just felt like busy work. You will not know your actual grade until it's on your transcript. She was an unprofessional teacher. I would not take her again.

Great person, but awful teacher. I learned next to nothing during lectures. Zybooks is the only tool that actually helps you learn. There are assignments every week and multiple group projects. Attendance is also a big part of your grade. Susan is a great person and even helped me raise my grade, however is just not a good teacher.

Harsh attendance taker when she doesnt even show up class on time. Work in class is not related to hw/lab due to unorganization. Canvas 3 weeks behind in class work at one point. Lagging email response. Cancelled class to work on her master's project and gave out only extra credit this semester for her master's research survey. Just a bad teacher.
She was very kind as a person, but as a professor, was hard to follow in this class.

Professor Nachawati was a very nice professor. She dropped a couple quizzes and lets you have cheat sheets for any exam. Her lectures were all over the place and couldn't focus on one topic. But she's really helpful during office hours. Quizzes every week, lots of homework, and we had, I think, 5-6 group projects.
It is not that difficult to get an A or B in this class. However, her class was not very helpful and I did not learn much from her lectures. Zybooks is where you will learn all the material.
I didn't like her at all. She complained too much. Her lectures were all over the place, so I stopped showing up. Her TA didn't know how to teach. He was kinda just there. This class was very boring.

She's a really nice and forgiving person for extensions and stuff, but I felt her lectures were all over the place. You can fully understand the content from the ZyBooks so read them as they're assigned and go ahead if you can. The labs were very confusing and a waste of time; they didn't serve as practice at all imo. Workload wasn't that bad.

Through the entire class, I passed with only doing zybooks(learn them) and barely paid attention in class. However, saying that doesn't mean it was an easy class. Participation whenever she remembers, messy lectures. Heavy work on zybooks, 3 mini projects, 2 mid terms(cheat sheets). Lots of discussions, playposits, and weekly quizzes.
Very confusing lectures, I recommend actually doing the zybooks and practicing a lot outside of class.

While Professor Nachawati was nice and caring, her lectures were pretty much useless. Only take this class if you have prior experience in coding, or you're willing to do self-studying with the provided zybooks, otherwise, look elsewhere.

Her lectures are not helpful and are often very confusing. She has a tendency to be unable to solve her own problems in class, and the structure of lectures is all over the place. The work assigned was pretty average in difficulty, so if you can teach yourself, you should be fine. I will say she is very caring, approachable, and answers email fast.
it's tough sadly, but it is what it is. terrible school.

Nachawati is not a good professor. She is a nice person, and cares about her students. However, her lectures are not enough for you to do well in the class. If you have no previous computer science knowledge, you are kind of screwed. Make sure to supplement your learning with resources outside of class if you actually want to learn anything.

As a complete beginner, was able to learn since ZyBooks helped. She often makes mistakes in lecture code which wastes time. Grading is slow and messy but talk to her and she'll try to fix. She's caring but assignments and rubric not specific enough since code needs to be. Make friends since they'll be more helpful, esp since projects can be hard.

This professor is a habitual liar. She lied about her grading scale, she lied about the curve, and she lied about the content of the exams. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. She can't speak English, she doesn't know the material well enough to teach it, and shes extremely sly.

The entirety of the class was us reading zybooks. Everyone who gave 5s is actually just her trying to save her rating tbh. If you do the work you'll get an A but she doesn't actually teach anything. You'll realize she tries to be nice to make up for her terrible teaching. She probably lied to get her degree. Props to her for lying so well.

By far one of the worst professors you can take. In 225 she lied about her grading system saying she'll curve exams or grading system but she doesn't. She often gets lost in her lectures and doesn't know how to do it. She will seem nice and that she helps but she actually doesn't. She skips out on office hours. I could write an essay on her.

If you have prior knowledge of python then it should be easy. however, if you are a complete beginner in the language then do not take this course. Prof does not really teach and your only form of actually learning something is from Zybook or from your peers. Grading in slow and frustrating due to the fact they arent clear on what they want

never again. only took this class because I had to. Prof is nice but every single assignment is confusing. TA was rude and biased in her grading. Literally worked with a friend (was allowed) and turned in our work. I got marked down so much and my friend who got the same answers got full points. TA's name was Aish. Stay away from this class.

This class will be easiest if you have prior knowledge of the basics of python or else you will be swarmed with all the online book lessons and projects she assigns every 2 weeks. For an intro class, her projects are very difficult however they aren't graded that strictly. You do have weekly quizzes and zyreads(lesson) which are very easy.

Susan is a very nice woman, but her lectures are very disorganized and made simple concepts confusing. On the final she said there were going to be 14 questions and then doubled it to 30 on the day of. Midterms/Finals review was not reflective of actual test. Midterms required more niche knowledge than was taught. Cheatsheets allowed on exams.
Personally I think she is an ok teacher and a nice person and she always explains more if you ask a question or go to office hours.
All you need to know about her is halfway through the final she said "I won't answer any more questions. You all overthink, just relax and trust yourselves."
Very caring woman, bur horrible professor. She lied about what would be on the final and if possible AVOID AT ALL COSTS! Wait a semester and take a different professor if you value your sanity.

While a decent person and clearly shows care in wanting students to pass, her actual skill in teaching leaves a lot to be desired. You'll find yourself lost as she goes on and on and doesn't give a moment to comprehend the information or apply it to her homework or quizzes. Silver lining is that she is somewhat generous on grades and curves it.

She is a very wholesome woman and if you open up to her through email she is very empathetic and offers help. 
Canvas uploads were confusing at times and assignments would be uploaded out of order, had no submission button, or duplicated etc. Attendance did not matter, but being present in labs did matter 100% for project info and lab work info.

Professor Nachawati is very loving, caring, and a terrible teacher all at the same time. As the previous reviews demonstrate, she does have a very alarming habit of lying, which no one wants in their university professor.

Very nice and respectful, but not as a teacher. Attempted to listen and learn from lectures from the beginning, but the material was unrelated to the work assigned and difficult to understand. Attendance was supposedly mandatory with random checks, but I practically ended up finding that showing up to class was a big waste of time. ZyBook carried

Incredibly nice lady however she CANNOT teach. Only reason I did well is bc I've taken a MASM class at CC. First 1.5 months are on binary, one month on digital logic gates, and about 1 week on actual assembly (MIPS). She takes easy subjects and makes them hard by not understanding how to teach them and making mistakes in poorly designed lectures

I'm currently taking this professor at a different college. I'm nearly 4 weeks from the end. She is nice but, doesn't teach well. Very unclear with her methods of using Masm/ASM for HW. Get your pcs ready to record yourself to explain your coding skills as this is 90% of your grade in the HW. Lockdown browser for quizzes and exams. My advice run.

She was lovely this year, I was scared to go into that class because of what people said about it, but they could not be more wrong. She is so kind and forgiving and she also teaches very well if you just LISTEN. All the time those who are complaining are too busy finding flaws rather than trying at all! I recommend her to everyone in CS.

Everyone that says she is a bad professor is just upset that it is not an easy A, those who love to be lazy and not do the work. She is very productive during lectures, tells fun stories, and is very positive even though people do not praise her enough. If you do your work honestly and pay attention to the lecture you will have the easiest time.

She doesn't have a very learning environment in her class and she doesn't teach effectively or any useful information. Her labs are a mess as all the lab instructors put in extra droboxes for each of their sections and I get missing assignments from classes that I'm not even enrolled in, honestly a horrible experience.
This professor, being as nice as she is, is a horrible teacher. She gives way too many assignments, doesn't grade them for months, and CANNOT teach. You will end up self-studying for everything....

Professor Nachawati is the worst. She is awful and I mean awful. Avoid if possible. She doesn't show up to office hours without warning, and has nocall noshowed to meetings that I have scheduled with her. The concepts in this class are not difficult, but she finds way to make them as hard as possible. She can rarely solve her own homework problems.
Such a sweet women but not a good teacher. This class made me change my major

Im not a cs major and have no prior experience but I found her class to be helpful. I went to her office hours and she is more than willing to help explain any confusion. She assigns a lot of hw but I think they are helpful and are applicable to the real world. Susan really cares for her students and if you want to learn to code, I recommend her.

She is extremely technologically illiterate, which is awful since this is a computer science course. She has no organzational skills and does not give you any information about the course ahead of time. She is kind but won't get back to you on almost anything. In person, she's alright, but online, she'll make you regret attending college.

Professor Susan is a very nice lady, but her class does not reflect her nice personality. Her lectures do not cover all the needed material to do projects, and homework is due before the lecture so you are pretty much going to teach yourself. She also assigns A LOT of work for a 3 unit course so be prepared. Is not flexible with deadlines.

Do not worry about what all the other students say about her. She's very sweet and is willing to help students. The labs she provided were not difficult at all and she was always more than happy to help clarify any confusion we had. Susan is an excellent professor! Glad I had her this past semester!

If you don't have any prior coding experience like me, this class is insane. I only did well because I got matched with partners that are CS majors and know other CS languages. There are 6 projects, 2 exams and a final, some quizzes, labs, and homework. It's A LOT of work. She is a very nice lady though, and really does want you to do well.

i don't want to take her class ever. if she take a exam she give us time 2 hr but exam question if we do it will be take around 5 hr. my all exam same think i got low grade my other sub all good but her class seriously, it's fine for her class when she teach but exam time. by chance if you take her class immediately drop the her class.

All things considered, the class itself is doable if you put in some effort in reading the book or watching the videos. I put in the bare minimum effort and got an A. That being said, while she's a nice enough lass, she's about as disorganized as a pile of laundry and her lectures are as useful as a chocolate fireguard on a hot summer day.

Susan is a caring person but not the best professor. Quizzes often have mistakes and her lectures are confusing. If it wasn't for my prior coding knowledge, I'd probably have a tougher time. Lab projects are time consuming but doable. Final project was not hard, but a lot of work. Overall, I'd learn thru ZyBooks and tune out of lectures altogether.

Had her for lab and she was extremely nice. Her lectures were very helpful and she would always answer questions from students. Very lenient on due dates, and tried very hard to help students understand material.
Words can't describe how bad this class was. I'm changing my majors. I lost my passion for coding.

This is 100% the worst professor I've ever had. Zyreads has taught me everything while the lectures are just restatements of zyreads except confusing and unbearably boring. Gives super unclear due dates and directions which will mess up your grade and wont accept late work The final project takes a whole week non-stop and is unrelated to coding :/

Susan Nachawati has to be one of the worst professors out there. She always makes a mistake on a quiz and doesn't even try and fix it afterwards unless students beg her too. She can't teach for her life so most of the learning will be on your own. I don't recommend this class to anyone and would rather jump off a building then take this class again

This was my first time trying a coding class and I do not think it fit the criteria of introductory at all. I feel that I have gained no knowledge and I am already changing majors. The lectures grow off of nothing and you have to figure out how to throw all these functions together. I do not recommend this for first time coders, save your money.

Dr. Nachawati is the worst instructor I've ever had. I advise anyone who is reading this to reconsider. The amount of work she asks from us is ridiculous. Never gives student's enough time. I found her to be very inconsiderate of her students. I talked to her on so many occasions, just for her to do the same thing again next week. FRUSTRATING!!!!!
Don't take her.
She is a very nice lady, however she is not the best teacher. All of her tests and quizzes have some questionable grammar and are confusing, and each one has at least one typo. Would not recommend.
You can tell she is really well educated on this subject, and she is one of the sweetest professors I've ever had
Caring person but not the best prof. ZyBooks, labs, weekly quizzes, 2 midterms, and 1 final. Gives ec for participating in lectures.

She doesn't read emails often. Lectures are often confusing and she seems to assign her assignments without actually looking at the assignment before to see if she taught it in class or not. Even though it is an online class she will not allow anyone to take the final exam outside of a 2 hour period which hurts a lot of my classmates' schedules.

If you want a professor who's going to inspire you to put in the work and effort to get the grade you deserve, than this is the one for you. She does a fantastic job at keeping us engaged and motivated to learn through trial and error. What set her apart as a human being was her dedication to teaching and encouraging persistence.

I have never met a more unorganized teacher. You would think after so many quizzes that there would not be any more mistakes but nope she is still careless and makes numerous mistakes. On too of that these mistakes impact your grade. Just dont take this class for your sanity. Super tough class for an introduction to programming.

Nachawati is an amazing person most of the time. Her accent is understandable, and she genuinely cares about your grade. However, her teaching methods are definitely lacking. The information in lectures is hard to understand, with her exams and labs the majority of the time misleading and filled with errors that definitely impact your grade. GL!!

This professor simply has no idea what she's doing. I've never seen a more clueless professor. Please just avoid at all costs because you will probably have to retake the class anyway. If there aren't any other options left for the class you're better off just taking another one and taking this one next sem.

I would not recommend this professor. I am also very suspicious of some reviews here, as others stated. Out of the 30+ students who signed up, four ended up finishing with passing grades. It speaks volumes that she has students passing at a 10% rate, all of which are coming in with coding experience. I recommend looking for another professor.

Susan Nachawati has to be one of the, if not the worst, and most unorganized professors at CSULB. I advise anyone who is looking to take her class to rethink their decision. PLEASE DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.

Very nice professor and truly does care about her students. But I often felt like she described things in a very circular manner, rushed over the hardest parts, assigned much more homework than was needed through various websites and labs, quizzes and tests often had spelling mistakes or grammatical mistakes that resulted in lower and unfair grades
Do not take this professor.

Cons: - Tests/quizzes have poor formatting/wording and may cause confusion. - You will learn more from the online readings than from her lectures. Pros: - She is very caring and kind, wants the best for everyone. - Gives lots of extra credit when needed. - She drops the two lowest quizzes.

She is a truly caring professor. I was really scared because of the bad reviews but she gives a lot of extra credit to make up you lowest quiz scores and always wants to help out like when you email her. Quizzes and midterms are not too bad too
Wants her students to succeed; if you need help, she is there for you.
Helpful and flexible with labs. Truly cares about her students.
She good but get ready go fo a lot of reading and HW exams kind of hard and a quiz every week.
Awful teacher.

Genuinely confused at all the reviews on here. Her lecturing style is very good and lets you know how every component in code works rather than leaving it up to you to figure out. If you put in effort, she'll work with you to give you a grade you deserve. Use office hours because her walking me through code helps me further understand everything.

Horrible/unorganized/unhelpful professor. Nachwati seriously takes the fun out of coding and computer science as a whole. She makes you pay for an online program that literally teaches you more than she teaches you. Please, whatever you do, DO NOT take her class.

Gives way too many labs, quizzes, and homework. CECS 174 is an intro class for programming, yet she constantly throws unnecessary, confusing labs at you expecting you to somehow know how to write the code clearly. The labs would be much more better if she could teach but no, she has no teaching abilities at all. Extremely inaccessible out of class.

Awful! Labs were too hard and not got any help either. I did the extra credit part but not got any points. I mailed about it to her but she didnt replied. She pulled out course from beachboard right after the day of exam. I failed to achieve A because she didnt gave me the extra credit points.

Awful Professor! Do not take her class. Her lectures are all over the place and she is very unprofessional. I have sent her 4 emails thus far and she did not reply to a single one. Do not take her unless it is your last option.

She's a nice person but teaching skill wise very disorganized. Her lab was her telling us stories to connect with the lesson but it was always so off topic it was hard to make a connection. Her labs did not keep up with the lectures. Her knowledge on coding is a bit outdated. Most assignments were of you uploading youtube videos of yourself.

Easily the most unprofessional, least helpful, and worst professor I've ever had. I'm not sure if it's the transition to online teaching, but I don't see that the professor has any form of planned teaching nor does she effectively communicate ANYTHING to the students.
